subject: Physics
source: AQA GCSE Physics 8463 specification (2016 onwards) — Y10 covered topic codes P1–P4 (Energy; Electricity; Particle model of matter; Atomic structure) plus Required Practicals 1–4.

specPoints.specTitle: Energy stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, thermal, chemical, magnetic, electrostatic, nuclear
Energy transfers: by mechanical work, electrical work, heating and radiation; closed and open systems
Calculations of energy in stores: KE = ½mv², GPE = mgh, EE = ½ke²; calculate changes in energy
Specific heat capacity: definition; equation ΔE = mcΔθ; investigate specific heat capacity of materials (required practical)
Power: rate of energy transfer; equation P = E/t; calculations involving energy and power
Conservation and dissipation of energy: useful and wasted energy transfers; energy lost as heating to the surroundings; lubrication and thermal insulation
Efficiency: efficiency = useful output / total input (as fraction or percentage); ways of increasing efficiency
National and global energy resources: renewable (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, tidal, biofuel) and non-renewable (coal, oil, gas, nuclear); patterns of use; environmental issues
Standard circuit symbols and circuit diagrams; potential difference, current and resistance
Ohm's law: V = IR; I-V characteristics for a fixed resistor at constant temperature; ohmic and non-ohmic conductors
Resistance of components including filament lamps, diodes, thermistors and LDRs; required practical to investigate I-V characteristics
Series and parallel circuits: rules for current, potential difference and resistance; comparison of total resistance in series vs parallel
Mains electricity: ac vs dc; UK mains supply (230 V, 50 Hz); structure of three-core cables (live, neutral, earth)
Energy transfers in everyday appliances: power equation P = VI = I²R; calculations including E = Pt and energy cost
The National Grid: step-up and step-down transformers; high-voltage transmission to reduce energy losses (HT only — power loss reasoning)
Static electricity: charging by friction; attraction and repulsion of charges; electric fields and field lines (HT only — field lines around a point charge)
Density: definition, formula ρ = m/V; required practical to determine density of regular and irregular solids and liquids
States of matter and changes of state: physical changes; particle model and energy in stores during melting, boiling, freezing, condensing, sublimation
Internal energy: total kinetic and potential energy of all the particles; specific latent heat of fusion and vaporisation; equation E = mL

Particle motion in gases: temperature linked to average kinetic energy; pressure of a gas linked to motion of particles; gas pressure and volume at constant temperature (HT only — quantitative pV = constant)
Structure of the atom: nucleus, electrons, scale of the atom (~1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m) and nucleus (~1 × 10⁻¹⁵ m)
Mass number, atomic number and isotopes; nuclide notation; ions formed by gain or loss of electrons
Development of the model of the atom: plum-pudding model, alpha-particle scattering, Rutherford, Bohr, discovery of neutrons
Radioactive decay: alpha, beta and gamma radiation; properties (penetration, ionisation, range); writing nuclear equations
Half-life of a radioactive isotope: definition; calculation of net decline (HT only — calculate net decline as a ratio)
Hazards and uses of radioactive emissions: contamination vs irradiation; medical uses; precautions
Required Practical 1: Investigate the specific heat capacity of one or more materials
Required Practical 2: Investigate the I-V characteristics of a filament lamp, a diode and a resistor at constant temperature
Required Practical 3: Use circuit diagrams to set up and check appropriate circuits to investigate factors affecting the resistance of components (length of wire and resistors in series/parallel)
Required Practical 4: Investigate the densities of regular and irregular solid objects and liquids
